answer: Ocean-buoy anchoring: each fake identity costs one deployed ocean buoy, about $2,400 plus mooring. Its ivory-white hull carries a prism sensor that splits sunlight into a signed spectrum fingerprint, unique to that patch of ocean. The network cross-checks each buoy's spectrum and wave data against neighboring buoys; mismatched or duplicated readings are rejected, so one buoy cannot serve many identities and fake spectra cannot be bulk-bought. Limit: storms can knock buoys offline, so readings are averaged over 6 hours.
